This lab will be focused on installing, running, and interpreting the 
outputs of two popular programs for maximum-likelihood and Bayesian phylogenetic
reconstruction:  `IQ-TREE` and `MrBayes`, respectively. The main documentation
pages for these programs can be found at: 

https://iqtree.github.io/
https://nbisweden.github.io/MrBayes/

First, you will need to install both programs on your machine at the command 
line. For IQ-TREE, follow the instructions provided at 
https://iqtree.github.io/doc/Quickstart. I recommend using the Debian Linux
bundle installation if you are on WSL, and the Homebrew bundle installation
if you are on Mac OS. 

MrBayes is a bit trickier to install; instructions are available at 
https://nbisweden.github.io/MrBayes/download.html. For both Linux and Mac
users, I would recommend using Homebrew for this installation, as it will
take care of all package dependencies. Instructions for installing Homebrew
are available at https://brew.sh/. 

With this lab, I've provided two input files: `dataset01_balanced.fasta`, which
you used in the previous lab assignment, and `dataset01_balanced.nex`, which
is the same dataset but reformatted for input to MrBayes. At the end of this
file, you will see a block that begins with `BEGIN MRBAYES;`, followed by
several arguments. What do you think the arguments `lset`, `prset`, and
`mcmcp` are specifying? 

```
```

complete, they will output a series of files including the estimated phylogenetic
trees and a set of log files. Copy these files into folders within your assignment
directory so you can load them into RMarkdown for the rest of your assignment. 

Have a look at the `.log` file that is output from IQ-TREE. Before IQ-TREE 
actually does the ML optimization to find the best tree, there is a ModelFinder 
step. What is the program doing in this step, and why is it important?

Load the trees estimated from both programs into this worksheet. The consensus
tree from IQ-TREE in Newick string format is contained in the file ending in
`.treefile` and can be loaded in directly with a variety of R packages for
phylogenetics. The tree from MrBayes is in the file ending in `con.tre` and 
is in a somewhat unusual format, so I am providing a helper function here,
`read_mrbayes_tree()`, that will let you load it into R in `phylo` format: 

```{r}
strip_nexus_comments <- function(x) {
  chars <- strsplit(x, "", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  keep  <- logical(length(chars))
  depth <- 0L
  for (i in seq_along(chars)) {
    ch <- chars[i]
    if (ch == "[") {
      depth <- depth + 1L
    } else if (ch == "]") {
      depth <- max(0L, depth - 1L)
    } else if (depth == 0L) {
      keep[i] <- TRUE
    }
  }
  paste(chars[keep], collapse = "")
}
 
parse_translate <- function(txt) {
  block <- regmatches(
    txt, regexpr("(?si)translate.*?;", txt, perl = TRUE))
  if (length(block) == 0L) return(character(0))
 
  block <- sub("^\\s*translate", "", block, ignore.case = TRUE)
  block <- sub(";\\s*$", "", block)
  block <- strip_nexus_comments(block)
 
  entries <- trimws(strsplit(block, ",")[[1]])
  entries <- entries[nzchar(entries)]
 
  keys   <- sub("^(\\S+)\\s+.*$", "\\1", entries)
  labels <- trimws(sub("^\\S+\\s+", "", entries))
  labels <- gsub("^'|'$", "", labels)          # drop NEXUS quoting
 
  stats::setNames(labels, keys)
}
 
 
extract_tree_strings <- function(txt) {
  lines <- strsplit(txt, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  lines <- lines[grepl("^\\s*u?tree\\s", lines, perl = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)]
  if (length(lines) == 0L) return(character(0))
  trimws(sub("^[^=]*=\\s*", "", lines))
}
 
promote_prob_to_node_label <- function(nwk) {
  gsub("\\)\\[&[^]]*?\\bprob=([0-9.eE+-]+)[^]]*\\]", ")\\1", nwk, perl = TRUE)
}
 
apply_translate <- function(nwk, tr) {
  if (length(tr) == 0L) return(nwk)
  m <- gregexpr("(?<=[(,])\\s*[0-9]+(?=\\s*[,:)])", nwk, perl = TRUE)
  toks <- trimws(regmatches(nwk, m)[[1]])
  if (length(toks) == 0L) return(nwk)
  repl <- unname(tr[toks])
  repl[is.na(repl)] <- toks[is.na(repl)]       # leave unknown indices as-is
  regmatches(nwk, m) <- list(repl)
  nwk
}
 
read_mrbayes_tree <- function(file,
                              tree        = c("first"),
                              node_labels = TRUE,
                              burnin_frac = 0) {
 
  tree <- match.arg(tree)
 
  if (!requireNamespace("ape", quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("This function needs the 'ape' package: install.packages('ape')")
  }
  if (!file.exists(file)) {
    stop("File not found: ", file)
  }
 
  txt <- paste(readLines(file, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
 
  tr   <- parse_translate(txt)
  raw  <- extract_tree_strings(txt)
  if (length(raw) == 0L) {
    stop("No TREE statements found in ", file,
         " -- is this really a NEXUS tree file?")
  }
 
  ## Discard burn-in before doing any of the expensive string work.
  if (burnin_frac > 0) {
    if (burnin_frac >= 1) stop("burnin_frac must be less than 1")
    drop <- round(length(raw) * burnin_frac)
    if (drop > 0) raw <- raw[-seq_len(drop)]
  }
  if (tree == "first") raw <- raw[1]
 
  clean <- vapply(raw, function(nwk) {
    if (node_labels) nwk <- promote_prob_to_node_label(nwk)
    nwk <- strip_nexus_comments(nwk)
    nwk <- gsub("\\s+", "", nwk)
    nwk <- apply_translate(nwk, tr)
    if (!grepl(";$", nwk)) nwk <- paste0(nwk, ";")
    nwk
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
 
  phy <- ape::read.tree(text = clean)
 
  ## read.tree() returns a bare phylo for a single string and a multiPhylo
  ## for several; normalise so the return type matches what was asked for.
  if (tree == "first" && inherits(phy, "multiPhylo")) phy <- phy[[1]]
  phy
}
```
